s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral arm weakness during a long-haul flight with a background of autoimmune hemolytic anemia
key_facts: 58-year-old woman
Developed right arm weakness 8 hours into a long-haul flight
Medical history of Coombs-positive autoimmune haemolytic anaemia
Presented with dehydration
Blood film showed auto-agglutination with macro-aggregates of red cells
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 119 mm/h
D-dimer was 24.7 nmol/L
Fibrinogen was 15.6 μmol/L
Renal function showed signs of dehydration
Elevated tumor markers
ECG and telemetry showed normal sinus rhythm
Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac chamber size and function
Brain MRI showed multiple small foci of restricted diffusion
Carotid ultrasound showed normal carotid and vertebral artery anatomy

shortlist.label: Embolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of unilateral arm weakness and multiple small foci of restricted diffusion on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated D-dimer, fibrinogen, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, with a background of autoimmune hemolytic anemia

shortlist.label: Cancer-associated thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated tumor markers and multiple echogenic targets with snowflake appearance on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia and elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, with a possible link to thrombosis

shortlist.label: Thrombotic microangiopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia and thrombocytopenia, with a background of autoimmune hemolytic anemia

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with right arm weakness, elevated D-dimer and fibrinogen, and multiple small foci of restricted diffusion on brain MRI, along with a history of autoimmune haemolytic anaemia and elevated tumor markers, suggests a prothrombotic state. The presence of auto-agglutination with macro-aggregates of red cells and a high erythrocyte sedimentation rate also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Embolic stroke
rejected.why: While the patient did have a stroke, the presence of multiple small foci of restricted diffusion and widespread microhaemorrhages suggests a more complex process than a simple embolic stroke.

rejected.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
rejected.why: The patient's coagulation studies did not show evidence of consumption of clotting factors or platelets, which is typical of DIC.

rejected.label: Cancer-associated thrombosis
rejected.why: While the patient had elevated tumor markers, there is no clear evidence of cancer, and the thrombotic events cannot be solely attributed to cancer.

rejected.label: Thrombotic microangiopathy
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and laboratory results do not show evidence of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia or thrombocytopenia, which are characteristic of TMA.
